params.body:
gentells.com is to say where a trend's signals come from: "From sources in 6 regions on 3 continents: DACH, Benelux, France, UK / Ireland, North America and East Asia." This sends the count with each trend, as `reading.origin`.

## How a signal's origin is found

`packages/core/trend-origin.mjs`, counted and not judged:

1. The country its adapter asked for (`adapter_meta.countryCode`): TikTok Creative Center and the other charts are read per country.
2. Otherwise the one region its source row names (`sources.region_hints`).
3. Otherwise nowhere: a source with no region, one that names several (an international title), a continent only, or Global.

Never the classifier's `region_tags`: those say what a signal is about, and they are a model's reading. Regions are the Standard's sub-regions (Benelux, DACH, East Asia, ...); continents are their parents.

Shape: `{regions: [{id, label, continent, signals}], continents, known, of}`, regions sorted by signals. `known` of `of` says how many of the listed signals have an origin, so the count is a floor. `null` when none is known; the site then says nothing. An error leaves it null and does not stop the projection, as with the graph.

## Tests

`test/trend-origin.test.mjs`: adapter country and source region counted, classifier tags never read, several regions or Global or a continent counted nowhere, continents counted, empty says nothing. Full suite 1617/1617, tsc clean.

The site side is a separate PR in gentells-site; either can merge first.
params.title: Projection: where a trend's signals come from, by region
